blocks.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
or = gold in heraldry
N and S, two points of the compass

annotation.surface: Someone finishing a sign by gilding its corners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Points' as compass points is a standing convention: any of N, S, E and W can be clued this way.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to adorn is to add ornament to something, making it more beautiful.

entries.clue: By which one makes up sauce on list (8,5)

definitions.note: the definition is a descriptive phrase: the piece of furniture by which one sits to make up

blocks.note: a salad dressing is a sauce
a table is a list of figures or items

annotation.surface: A chef's order sheet: the sauce written on the list.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Makes up' looks like composing a sauce, but it means putting on make-up, which is done sitting by a dressing table.
annotation.definitionFit: The mirrored bedroom furniture where people sit to apply cosmetics is described by what happens beside it.

entries.clue: Royal Engineers said to go free (7)

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the next piece counts by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: RE is the standard abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to leave is to go; 'said' turns the sound into a different spelling

annotation.surface: Soldiers being told they may be released.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the second half is heard: RE plus a sound like 'leave' gives RELIEVE.
annotation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a burden or duty is to release them from it, a plain synonym.

indicators.note: berserk means wild and out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A gun that turns a hunting party into a frenzy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go berserk' reads as one phrase, but 'go' belongs to the fodder: HUNTS GO rearranges to SHOTGUN.
annotation.definitionFit: The answer names a particular firearm firing pellets, so the general category stands for it.

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: AB = able seaman
a duct is a channel for fluid or air

annotation.surface: A sailor from Shanghai standing beside a waterway.
annotation.walkthrough: Shanghai looks like the Chinese city, but here it is a verb: to shanghai is to kidnap someone into service as a sailor.
annotation.definitionFit: To shanghai someone is to force or trick them aboard a ship, which is kidnapping.

blocks.note: used as it stands
a shade of colour, as in a paler variety of blue

annotation.surface: Asking which colour of make-up to choose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make up' reads as cosmetics, but it is the verb: to make up for a wrong.
annotation.definitionFit: Both mean to make amends for a wrong or offence, with the answer taking 'for' after it.

indicators.note: the answer is found lying in the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of 'inside' run on into the first three of 'monastery'

annotation.surface: A devil lurking in a holy house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inside' looks like the indicator, but it is part of the source: its last two letters start the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a malevolent supernatural being, a devil or fiend.

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a standard is a flag or banner
a ration is a fixed quota

annotation.surface: A report on how much fuel each fire is allowed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as normal, but here it is the military banner, FLAG.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal word for a large, destructive blaze that spreads over buildings or land.

blocks.note: well = in good health
a to-do is a fuss or commotion

annotation.surface: A rich, lively party.
annotation.walkthrough: A to-do, meaning a fuss, supplies the second half.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for wealthy, comfortably off: the rich are described this way.

entries.clue: After short day, king joins brother (4)

indicators.note: short means abbreviated, so the day is cut to three letters
the king comes after the day in the answer

blocks.note: the abbreviation of Monday
K = king in chess notation

annotation.surface: A king joining a religious order at the start of the week.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brother' is the title of a member of a religious order.
annotation.definitionFit: Members of male religious orders are addressed by this title, so it stands for one of them.

indicators.note: back means read in the opposite direction
in says the letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: the second to fifth letters of the city

annotation.surface: Dogs returning to Finland.
annotation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a district in East London, so 'Dogs' is one example of an isle, flagged by 'eg'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a London district named after a peninsula in the Thames is one instance.

entries.clue: Insect found on a putting surface? (8)

definitions.text: Insect found on a putting surface?

blocks.note: the real meaning: a small plant-sucking aphid
the surface reading: a bug that has landed on a golf course's smooth lawn by the hole

annotation.surface: A bug that has landed on a golf green.
annotation.walkthrough: A fly on a putting green would be a green fly; the real greenfly is an aphid found on plants.
annotation.definitionFit: The aphid pest of gardens takes its name from its colour, and a golf green is where putting happens.

indicators.note: the question asks whether we heard right, pointing to sound

blocks.note: one after another, in order

annotation.surface: Someone checking they heard a prison order correctly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In turn' and INTERN sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: To hold someone, especially an enemy alien in wartime, in a camp without trial is a kind of confinement.

blocks.note: G = good
a range is a large kitchen stove

annotation.surface: Recommending a fine cooker for a manor kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: A grange is a British country house, often with farm buildings.
annotation.definitionFit: A British word for a rural manor with its farm buildings, originally a monastery's outlying farm.

indicators.note: the outer words cover the answer, which lies inside them

blocks.note: the last three letters of the first word and the first four of the second

annotation.surface: A park ranger told off for smothering a plant.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of 'Ranger' and the start of 'berated'.
annotation.definitionFit: A bright daisy-like flower from southern Africa, popular with florists: one specific plant.

blocks.note: the first man in Genesis
the ant is a social insect and a worker

annotation.surface: A stubborn man paired with a council caseworker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' reads as a job in welfare, but it is an ant, which lives in colonies and works.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: refusing to be persuaded or change one's mind, unyielding.

indicators.note: the ship carries R within it

blocks.note: a steamship
R = right; it goes after the second letter of the ship

annotation.surface: A vessel flying the proper flag.
annotation.walkthrough: Crosswords usually make a ship SS; here the whole vessel type is wanted, and 'right' is simply R.
annotation.definitionFit: A long narrow flag flown from a masthead, tapering like a ribbon.

entries.clue: Discard, not initially, then throw out (5)

blocks.note: to discard something as unwanted

annotation.surface: Instructions for clearing out junk.
annotation.walkthrough: REJECT loses its R to become EJECT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to expel or force someone or something to leave a place.

indicators.note: force comes first, before the R

blocks.note: to make someone do something is to force them
R = right

annotation.surface: A film producer who wants the right amount of power up front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right force first' tempts you to put R at the front; 'first' applies to 'force', so MAKE leads.
annotation.definitionFit: Anyone who manufactures or creates goods is one, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: A drain at the earliest opportunity (inits) (4)

blocks.note: used as it stands
to sap is to drain energy

annotation.surface: A plumber being asked to unblock a drain urgently.
annotation.walkthrough: '(inits)' warns that the answer is initials: ASAP stands for 'as soon as possible'.
annotation.definitionFit: Initials for 'as soon as possible', meaning without delay.

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: take the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

annotation.surface: Hesitation about whether to play a standard instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regular' reads as an adjective describing the instrument, but it picks out every second letter of 'Doubt over'.
annotation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind of the orchestra, so one specific musical kind.

entries.clue: I take pet out and persevere (4,2,2)

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A dog owner doggedly walking the pet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take pet out' reads as a walk, but 'out' works on 'I take pet'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for continuing to work at something despite difficulty.

blocks.note: AC = alternating current
the tone of a scene is its mood
